title: Tighten a row's coefficients

blocks.text: A crew-allocation model has knapsack rows $`\sum_j a_j x_j \le b`$ with $`a_j > 0`$ and every $`x_j \in \{0, 1\}`$ free. Before the search, presolve should tighten them, so the LP relaxation gives a better bound with the same 0-1 plans.
Write `tighten(coefs, rhs)` in `tighten.py`. Go through the variables in sorted order of their names. For each variable $`k`$, with the row as it is at that moment, compute

and if $`d > 10^{-9}`$, replace $`a_k`$ by $`a_k - d`$ and $`b`$ by $`b - d`$. Return the pair `(new_coefs, new_rhs)`: a new dict, with the dict you were given left as it was. Each later variable sees the row after the earlier changes.

from __future__ import annotations

EPS = 1e-9


def tighten(coefs: dict[str, float], rhs: float) -> tuple[dict[str, float], float]:
    """Coefficient tightening of  sum a_j x_j <= rhs  over free binaries with a_j > 0."""
    new = dict(coefs)
    for k in sorted(new):
        most = sum(new.values())
        d = rhs - (most - new[k])
        if d > EPS:
            new[k] -= d
            rhs -= d
    return new, rhs


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(tighten({"a": 4, "b": 3, "c": 3}, 8))

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from tighten import tighten

# Crew rows over free binaries.
row = {"east": 7, "north": 2, "west": 3}
coefs, rhs = tighten(row, 8)
print("row 7e + 2n + 3w <= 8 becomes:", coefs, "<=", rhs)
print("row passed in afterwards:", row)
print("row 3x + 3y + 2z <= 7 becomes:", tighten({"x": 3, "y": 3, "z": 2}, 7))
print("row 2x + 5y <= 6 becomes:", tighten({"x": 2, "y": 5}, 6))
